hypothesis: BGK-PBE is a geological hypothesis: basement gravity-gradient edges, radiometric potassium/K-eTh alteration, and geodetic dilatation could jointly indicate concealed geothermal faults near piedmont-basin transitions. The checked-in raster does not test this hypothesis; its fields and footprint are synthetic placeholders.
mechanism: The archived generator synthesizes NNE linear pulses, a hand-coded transition band, sinusoidal pseudo-gravity, filtered random pseudo-potassium, and coordinate-derived pseudo-dilatation inside an approximate ellipse. These are not values read from the competition stack or USGS data. The raster has 6,178 hard cells (>0.5) and 8,794 total positive cells (>0).
mimic: Plutonic intrusive margins, lithologic contacts, playa/shoreline boundaries, drainage, and arbitrary linear cartographic patterns could mimic faults. The synthetic raster does not model or suppress these mimics using real geology.
